task: Milestone 0 for the koala authority enforce product track: record an explicit PD-2 decision that introduces a future isolated headless authority-enforce runner namespace while keeping ordinary koala as a thin workflow client, then add mechanical checks that prevent local/shadow transport evidence or accepted true responses from being presented as receipt-backed L2+ authority.
outcome: When this story is done, a future agent can run the relevant authority boundary tests and read docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md, then say: "好了，普通 koala 还是 workflow thin client；只有未来 koala authority enforce 子系统在具备 signed envelope 和 verified server receipt 后才能声称 L2+。Milestone 0 没有实现 actor key、job claim、provider execution、full envelope 或 receipt verification。"
facts: Existing PD-1 records Koala CLI as a thin local/shadow lifecycle client and defers first-class enforce-mode authority work.
Existing authority-boundary classifier already distinguishes thin-client transport acceptance from receipt-backed L2+ classification.
Python authority policy discovery has been implemented in the cord-team repo, but this Orchestrate story must not mutate that repo.
Mac Runner remains a production execution plane and is not replaced by this work.
constraints: Do not implement actor-key registration, runner heartbeat, job claiming, provider execution, full EvidenceEnvelope submission, or receipt verification in Milestone 0.
Do not let existing workflow evidence handlers claim production L2+ authority.
All story/checklist/evidence metadata must be updated through Koala commands, not direct story-file edits.
Claude Code CLI performs implementation work; Codex supervises and verifies.
unknowns: Whether later milestones will keep nested command syntax or use flat Koala command names depends on the current CLI command registry design.
The exact Python authority policy fields for Milestone 1 should be re-read from the live /v1/authority/policy contract before implementation.
